why.text: The vineyard is sunlit all day at 870 m, and its big day-night temperature contrast makes ripening very slow.

styles.text: Red wine only.

climate.text: Sun all day on the vineyard. A very high heat sum, with a big day-night contrast, makes ripening very slow.

soil.text: Sandy loam with limestone and a basic pH.

altitude.text: The vineyard site is at 870 m.

tastes.text: Picota red, no signs of age. Red and black fruit (plum, blackberry, blueberry), thyme and Mediterranean scrub. Fleshy, full body; ripe, sweet-tasting tannins.

why.text: Spring and summer water stress, with high temperatures and evapotranspiration, gives intense aromas. The considerable temperature range gives marked colour intensity.

styles.text: White, rosado and red wines, plus sweet liqueur wines (Moscatel), aromatic sparkling and semi-sparkling wines.

climate.text: Mediterranean: mild temperatures all year, hot spring and summer with water stress, and a wide day-night range.

soil.text: Brown limy soils with poorly developed humus layers and a silty-sand texture.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to golden, fresh and fruity. Rosés: raspberry, strawberry, redcurrant or salmon pink. Reds: purple, garnet, cherry or ruby, good fruit. Aged wines: tile-red tones, fruit and wood in balance.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: White, rosé or red; sweet and rich, most intense from Moscatel.

styles.name: Espumoso aromático de calidad
styles.text: White, rosé or red; clean, intense aromas, fresh, well-integrated carbonic gas.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Fresh, fruity and intense, with well-integrated carbonic gas.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Fruit and wood in balance on the nose; well structured, with good retronasal sensations.

why.text: Bobal's polyphenol load and high natural acidity give intense red, full-bodied wines. The limy soils bring quite intense floral and white-fruit aromas to the whites.

styles.text: Reds led by Bobal, whites, deeply coloured rosados, sparkling and semi-sparkling wines, low-alcohol wines and late-harvest liqueur wines.

climate.text: Very sunny, with little risk of fungal disease, so grapes ripen fully and can be harvested very late.

soil.text: Mostly loam, often stones and gravel on medium slopes; generally alkaline with high total and active lime, poor in organic matter.

tastes.text: Reds: intense red with violet tints; black and red fruit, riper with time; full-bodied, balanced acidity. Whites: yellow, floral and white-fruit aromas, fresh. Rosés: lively pink; red fruit, strawberry in Bobal.

styles.name: Vino de baja graduación
styles.text: Fruity wines, fresh and harmonious; white, rosé or red.

styles.name: Espumoso aromático de calidad
styles.text: Yellow; fruit aromas of the grapes used; slightly sweet.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Varietal aromas; light and fresh on the palate.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: White, rosado or red; unctuous, with very balanced acidity and sugar.

why.text: The sloping vineyard drains well and gives the vines better sun exposure, which helps ripening and the polyphenols behind colour and body.

styles.text: Red and white wines.

climate.text: Continental with a Mediterranean influence; 450 mm of rain a year.

soil.text: Cenozoic limy deposits and marls with high active lime; homogeneous sandy clay loam, basic pH, low organic matter; gentle 7 % slopes at about 700 m.

tastes.text: Red: deep cherry; ripe grape, blackberry, raspberry, plum, forest floor and oak; velvety, ripe tannins. White: straw yellow; white and exotic fruit, pineapple, mango; rich, fresh finish.

why.text: Monastrell grows on a high, dry plateau with deep, limy soils. It gives fleshy, warm reds with good balance.

styles.text: Fleshy, warm reds; also whites, rosados, sparkling wines and sweet liqueur wines.

climate.text: Dry continental: hot summers, very cold winters, about 300 mm of rain a year and over 3,000 hours of sun.

soil.text: Limy, deep and well drained, very low in organic matter.

altitude.text: The vineyards lie on rolling ground between 535 and 870 m.

tastes.text: Whites: pale straw with green glints to golden. Rosés: raspberry and cherry pink with purple tints. Reds: violet cherry with garnet tones; fruity, fleshy, warm, tannic yet soft, balanced, high extract.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Sweet, full-bodied and unctuous, well balanced, with a very long finish.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Whites golden-yellow, rosés raspberry pink, reds violet cherry; persistent, long finish.

why.text: Hardy Monastrell is suited to drought and strong summer heat. It makes broad, fleshy reds with ripe-fruit aroma.

styles.text: Monastrell reds and rosados (at least 85% Monastrell for the varietal wines); whites; sweet versions; Monastrell liqueur wines.

climate.text: Clearly continental despite the nearby Mediterranean: dry, barely 300 l/m² of rain a year, summer highs at times well over 40 ºC, winter lows near -10 ºC, mean 16 ºC, about 3,000 hours of sun.

soil.text: Brown and reddish-brown limy soils, loam to sandy loam, loose, stony, poor in organic matter, usually deep, with good water retention; vineyards at 320 to 900 m.

tastes.text: Reds: blue-violet to tile red (ochre in sweet), red and black fruit, tannic, balanced acidity. Rosados: raspberry pink to onion skin, red fruit. Whites: steely to amber, white fruit. Sweet wines: dried-fruit notes, sweetness over acidity.

styles.name: Jumilla Monastrell
styles.text: Made with at least 85% Monastrell.

styles.name: Jumilla dulce
styles.text: Sweet red, white or rosado; sweetness dominates acidity, dried-fruit notes, reds may reach ochre.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Fortified red, Monastrell only, 15 to 22% vol; black and dried fruit, tannic.

why.text: Humid sea air meets dry, hard calcareous ground here. Together they make the wines fresher and subtler than those of inland neighbours.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, aged "añejo" wines, Fondillón, liqueur wines and sparkling wines.

climate.text: Strong summer sun at ripening, tempered by humidity from the Mediterranean; drier and milder than continental areas.

soil.text: Dry, hard calcareous soils and rock; the document calls the soils rich.

tastes.text: Reds: ruby to violet, fresh red fruit when young; cherry, ripe fruit and balsamic notes when aged; structured. Whites: pale yellow to amber, white flowers, citrus. Rosés: salmon to pink, fruity.

styles.name: Fondillón
styles.text: Red; mahogany to coppery; ripe and dried fruit, well-integrated wood, slightly sweet.

styles.name: Vino añejo
styles.text: Mahogany tones; intense, oaky; long, structured finish.

styles.name: Vino noble
styles.text: Cherry tones with orange rims; intense, oaky; long aftertaste.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: White, rosado or red; ripe fruit, raisins, white flowers; sweet.

why.text: Monastrell makes up 80% of plantings, on soil where limestone predominates, in a dry climate at altitude. It gives broad, fleshy, deeply coloured reds.

styles.text: Mostly Monastrell reds, young or oak-aged; dry whites, rosados, sparkling and liqueur wines.

climate.text: A dry climate, with altitude as an influence.

tastes.text: Whites: dry and clean. Rosés: violet pink to salmon. Reds: violet red to ruby when young, tile-red when aged; varietal aroma, structured, balanced tannin and acidity; aged ones show maturity.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Violet to tile red; ripe, candied fruit, balsamic, spice; unctuous, long sweet finish.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Intense, fresh, fruity aromas.

why.text: At 720 m and open to cold north winds, this is one of the coolest sites in its district.

styles.text: Reds (blends, or Cabernet Franc alone): at least 5 months in oak. White: barrel-fermented. Rosado: macerated in oak barrels.

climate.text: Continental with Mediterranean influence. Rain is 350 to 400 mm, mostly in September. There are about 3,000 sun hours a year. Big day-night swings at ripening.

soil.text: Alkaline loam (pH 8 to 9), about 1% organic matter. Active limestone 7 to 21%. Limestone layer at 30 cm.

altitude.text: Vineyard at 720 m, among the coldest sites in the district.

tastes.text: Reds: intense red; fruity, balsamic, ripe tannins, chocolate, mineral. Cabernet Franc: violet red; black fruit, herbs. White: straw; floral, fruity, oak. Rosado: deep pink; red fruit, oak; fresh.

styles.name: Tinto multivarietal
styles.text: Grapes made apart; all reds: at least 14 days on skins, 5 months in oak.

styles.name: Tinto monovarietal (Cabernet Franc)
styles.text: Single-grape red; black fruit and herbs, with fruit ahead of oak notes.

styles.name: Blanco
styles.text: White fermented in oak barrels after skin contact; stored in steel or concrete.

styles.name: Rosado
styles.text: Rosé from four grapes; at least three weeks of maceration in oak barrels.

why.text: An airy microclimate with moderated extremes and loose, permeable limestone soils give healthy, slowly ripened grapes and long-lived wines.

styles.text: Reds, young or oak-aged. Whites and rosados. Quality sparkling wines, white and rosado.

climate.text: Continental, slightly Mediterranean. About 430 mm of rain and over 3,000 sun hours a year. Summer days reach 33 °C, nights 12 °C.

soil.text: Sandy to sandy-loam, loose and shallow, over porous limestone 2 to 4 m down. High in carbonates; pH 8.2 to 8.3.

altitude.text: At 690 m, sheltered to the north by the Juan Navarro range (1,200 m).

tastes.text: Reds: purple-red to cherry when young, garnet to ruby when aged; red fruit, balsamic herbs; soft tannins. Whites: lemon yellow with gold glints; stone fruit, citrus, herbs. Sparkling: fine bubbles; toast, butter.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad blanco
styles.text: Old-gold sparkling white; white flowers, stone fruit, citrus, toast, butter; fine bubbles.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad rosado
styles.text: Pale pink sparkling rosé; cherry, raspberry, citrus, bread; delicate bubbles.

styles.name: Vino tinto
styles.text: Red, young or oak-aged; aged ones show toast, spice, smoke and dairy notes.

styles.name: Vino rosado
styles.text: Pale pink with orange glints; red and stone fruit; smoke and spice after oak.

why.text: A shallow water table softens day-night swings and raises humidity, which keeps the acidity balanced.

styles.text: Oak-aged reds in four ageing grades; white Chardonnay fermented in new oak; rosado mostly from Bobal.

climate.text: About 430 mm of rain on 52 rainy days and 2,600 hours of sun. A shallow water table softens day-night swings.

soil.text: Mainly brown limestone soils on mostly Miocene ground; 38% total limestone, pH about 8.5.

tastes.text: Crianza: cherry red; fruit and spice, Mediterranean scrub; sweet tannins. Reserva: sour-cherry red with tile hints; vanilla; big volume, dry finish. Gran Reserva: garnet; very ripe fruit, toasted oak. Rosado: strawberry red; fruity, floral. White: straw; fruity.

styles.name: Vino tinto madurado en barrica
styles.text: Red kept in oak under 6 months; red-fruit and woodland aromas.

styles.name: Vino tinto Crianza
styles.text: Red aged at least 6 months in oak; fruit and spice with sweet tannins.

styles.name: Vino tinto Reserva
styles.text: Red aged at least 12 months in oak; soft and full, with a dry finish.

styles.name: Vino tinto Gran Reserva
styles.text: Red aged at least 18 months in oak; very ripe fruit and toasted oak.
